examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Rational Functions With a Repeated Factor and Another Factor
examples.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}-5x+8}{(x-3)^{2}(x+1)} & =\frac{A}{(x-3)}+\frac{B}{(x-3)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-3)^2(x+1)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-5x+8 & =A(x-3)(x+1)+B(x+1)+C(x-3)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $C$ and solve for $B\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}3({3}^{2})-5(3)+8 & =A(3-3)(3+1)+B(3+1)+C(3-3)^{2} \\ 20 & =B(4) \\ B & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=-1,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-1)^{2}-5(-1)+8 & =A(-1-3)(-1+1)+B(-1+1)+C(-1-3)^{2} \\ 16 & =C{(-4)}^{2} \\ C & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $B$ and $C,$ we can solve for $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}3({0}^{2})-5(0)+8 & =A(0-3)(0+1)+B(0+1)+C(0-3)^{2} \\ 8 & =-3A+B+9C \\ 8 & =-3A+5+9(1) \\ 3A & =6 \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{3x^2-5x+8}{(x-3)^2(x+1)} = \dfrac{2}{(x-3)} +\dfrac{5}{(x-3)^2} +\dfrac{1}{(x+1)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}-5x+8}{(x-3)^{2}(x+1)}\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{(x-3)}+\frac{5}{(x-3)^{2}}+\frac{1}{(x+1)})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\text{d}x+5\int \frac{1}{(x-3)^{2}}\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+5(-\,\frac{1}{x-3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|-\frac{5}{(x-3)}+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K\,,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{x+3}{(x-5)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x-5}+\frac{B}{(x-5)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-5)^{2}$ and get

$$
x+3=A(x-5)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=5,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5+3 & =A(5-5)+B \\ B & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+3 & =A(0-5)+8 \\ 3 & =-5A+8 \\ 5A & =5 \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{x+3}{(x-5)^{2}}=\frac{1}{x-5}+\frac{8}{(x-5)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x+3}{(x-5)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{x-5}+\frac{8}{(x-5)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x-5}\,\text{d}x+8{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x-5)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-5|\,{|}_{0}^{1}-\frac{8}{x-5}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-5|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0-5|)-(\frac{8}{1-5}-\frac{8}{0-5}) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡5)-(-2-(-\frac{8}{5})) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{5})+\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
